reviewers.summary: The escaped-name check closes the reported filter-name bypass. The page-text guard still checks the limit after PdfPig has produced the mapped letter values, so the prior resource-exhaustion finding remains.

findingList.message: OWASP A06:2025 (Insecure Design): the precheck still materializes PdfPig letter values before enforcing the text bound, leaving the prior font-mapping resource-exhaustion risk reachable.

evidence.codePathTraced: ParseCore passes page.Letters values to CanMaterializePageText before calling page.Text, but PdfPig must produce the page letters and their mapped values for that enumeration. The limit is checked only after those values have been materialized.
evidence.failureScenario: A PDF within the 10 MB input limit and 8 MiB decoded-stream limit uses a font mapping that expands repeated glyphs into very long strings. PdfPig can allocate the expanded letter values while evaluating getTextParts(page), exhausting API process memory before CanMaterializePageText can reject the page. The added test substitutes synthetic text parts, so it does not exercise this PdfPig path.

reviewers.summary: The escaped-filter check addresses the prior filter-name bypass. The text-size guard still does not prevent resource exhaustion during PdfPig letter materialization.

findingList.message: The new text-size guard checks page.Letters only after PdfPig materializes the letters. Bound extraction before those allocations occur.

evidence.codePathTraced: ParseCore calls getTextParts(page), whose production delegate accesses page.Letters before CanMaterializePageText can inspect the returned values. PdfPig materializes page letters during that access, so the size check runs after extraction allocations have begun.
evidence.failureScenario: A PDF within the input and decoded-stream limits uses a font mapping that expands glyphs into very large text. Accessing page.Letters can allocate that text before the guard rejects it, exhausting API process resources. This leaves the prior resource-exhaustion finding reachable (OWASP A06:2025).

reviewers.summary: The page-text check still occurs after PdfPig materializes the page's letters, leaving the previously reported resource-exhaustion path reachable.

findingList.message: The text bound is checked after PdfPig materializes page.Letters, so oversized glyph expansion can still exhaust API resources before rejection.

evidence.codePathTraced: ParseCore calls getTextParts(page) before CanMaterializePageText checks the accumulated text size. The default getTextParts accesses page.Letters, whose letter collection PdfPig has already materialized while constructing the page.
evidence.failureScenario: A presenter submits a PDF within the compressed-stream limit whose font mappings expand its glyphs into very large letter values. PdfPig can allocate the expanded letter collection before CanMaterializePageText rejects it, exhausting API process memory (OWASP A06:2025, Insecure Design).
